Attack rates and relative risks by exposure

Source: R/summaries.R
phw_risk_table.Rd

The standard outbreak investigation table: for each exposure (a food, a setting, a risk factor) and each of its levels, the number of people, the number who became cases, the attack rate, and the relative risk against the reference level with a confidence interval and Fisher's exact p-value.

Usage

phw_risk_table(
  data,
  exposures,
  outcome,
  labels = list(),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  digits = 1,
  p_value = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per person.

exposures

Exposure columns, chosen as in dplyr::select(), e.g. c(item_a, item_b). Logical or yes/no columns work best; the first level (or FALSE/"No") is the reference.

outcome

Outcome column: logical, 0/1 or yes/no (case = TRUE, 1 or "Yes").

labels

Named list of display names for exposures.

conf_level

Confidence level.

digits

Decimal places.

p_value

Add a p-value column?

Value

A phw_summary data frame.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(item_a = sample(c("Yes", "No"), 120, TRUE),
                item_b = sample(c("Yes", "No"), 120, TRUE))
d$ill <- rbinom(120, 1, ifelse(d$item_a == "Yes", 0.5, 0.15))
phw_risk_table(d, c(item_a, item_b), ill,
               labels = list(item_a = "Item A", item_b = "Item B"))
#>  Exposure People Cases Attack rate (%) Relative risk       95% CI p-value
#>    Item A     NA    NA              NA                                   
#>        No     61     7            11.5 1 (reference)                     
#>       Yes     59    27            45.8          3.99 1.88 to 8.45  <0.001
#>    Item B     NA    NA              NA                                   
#>        No     58    14            24.1 1 (reference)                     
#>       Yes     62    20            32.3          1.34 0.75 to 2.39    0.42
#> p-values from Fisher's exact test.
